- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Overshoots after sharp upward spikes in history (e.g., after 75+ values), then corrects with a downward bias in later days.
- Underestimates during periods of strong downward momentum (e.g., 68–70 range) — model fails to recognize mean reversion or risk of price drop.
- Forecast lags behind true price movements by 1–3 days, particularly in the middle of the 30-day window.
- Model exhibits high variance in later days (e.g., 25–30) with erratic spikes — likely overfitting to recent noise or ignoring macro trends.
- When history includes a recent high, model tends to overreact with a peak forecast, then undercorrects — suggesting poor smoothing or lack of decay in momentum.
- Model underestimates true price when history shows a strong downward trend (e.g., 70–72 range) — fails to recognize risk of reversal or volatility clustering.
- Forecast mean is typically 1–2 points higher than true mean — suggests systematic upward bias, possibly due to momentum or volatility skew.
